purpose: Teach: 伊達/沸い/問答/贈ら/リスナー/河原/ペダル/バク

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、伊達メガネ、絶対、流行ったわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When we were young, you remember—those fake glasses were actually everywhere. Your grandmother remembers that, doesn't she?
lines.style: Nostalgic, reaching back through time. Warm but slightly uncertain—testing if the memory lands. Gentle upswing on the question, inviting her into the shared past.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祭りで、絶対、観客、絶対、沸いた、絶対、思い出、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I do. When we were young, the festivals would come alive—everyone so excited, so full of life. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Soft and alive with remembered joy. Her voice opens like she's stepping back into that moment. Unhurried, as if savoring each image as it surfaces.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、問答、絶対、無用、絶対、お父さん、絶対、男気あったよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: And your father—he had such spirit back then. Real backbone. You remember how he was, don't you?
lines.style: Quieter now, with respect underneath. The words land deliberately, like he's placing each memory carefully. Slight pause before her name, giving weight to the asking.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃんから、絶対、結婚指輪、絶対、贈られた、絶対、嬉しい、絶対、思い出、覚えてる、あなた?本気で、絶対、本気、絶対、本気で。
lines.en: Your grandfather gave me my wedding ring back then. I was so happy. I remember it so clearly—how could I ever forget something like that?
lines.style: Voice softens into tenderness. Almost touching the memory as she speaks. The final phrase is quietly certain—not a question but a statement of what matters. Steady and sure.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お祖母ちゃん、本気で、絶対、ラジオの、絶対、リスナー、絶対、ね、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: You were always listening to the radio, weren't you? I can still picture it. You remember, don't you?
lines.style: Gentle and slightly amused by the image. Affectionate teasing underneath. A little reaching—checking if the memory is still there between them, still shared.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、河原で、絶対、二人で、絶対、デート、絶対、したわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で、絶対、思い出
lines.en: We used to go on dates down by the river, just the two of us. Those were real days. You haven't forgotten, have you?
lines.style: Tender and matter-of-fact. Not dramatic—the simplicity itself carries all the meaning. Her voice stays warm and close, like she's sitting right beside him with this.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、私、絶対、自転車のペダル、絶対、よく、漕いだわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: I remember pedaling that bicycle everywhere back then. Working so hard at it. Do you remember how I was?
lines.style: Self-aware affection in the voice. A small laugh hidden underneath—gentle self-mockery mixed with real pride. The question is warm, not seeking reassurance but inviting her to see him as he was.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、家族で、絶対、動物園、絶対、バクを、絶対、見た、覚えてる、あなた?本気で、絶対、思い出
lines.en: We all went to the zoo together—remember? We saw the tapir. That whole day, that whole memory is still so clear to me.
lines.style: Close and intimate. Her voice carries the weight of time held gently. Not wistful but grounded—these are moments she has carried with her. Unhurried, certain.
